newsitem.title: USA: Sovereign acquires Fleet auto unit.
newsitem.headline: Sovereign acquires Fleet auto unit.

text.p: Sovereign Bancorp Inc said Wednesday that it had signed a definitive pact to acquire Fleet Financial Group Inc's automobile finance division, a move that would make it one of the largest auto lenders in the Northeast.
Soverign said it expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to its earnings, adding about $0.02 per share in 1997 and about $0.08 per share in 1998.

Fleet Auto holds about $2 billion of indirect auto loans, dealer floor plan loans and auto lessor loans. The division has originated between $700 million to $1.0 billion in new loans annually over the past few years and serves customers in New Jersey, New York and in several New England states.
Sovereign said it expects to significantly grow the business, by both increasing its current five percent share and by expanding into Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maryland and Virginia.
As part of the deal, Sovereign said it has agreed to offer employment to substantially all of the division's employees.

The deal lets Soverign buy the business at a discount, which Sovereign said it will use in part to create initial reserves for possible loan losses of about $19 million. It said Fleet will transfer no loan loss reserves to it.

Sovereign said the Fleet acquisition and the $325 million stock acquisition of Bankers Corp announced in February will make it a significant regional bank in mortgage lending, consumer lending and small business lending.
Both acquisitions are expected to close in the third quarter.
Sovereign said it will have about $2.5 billion of its loan portfolio in consumer loans and about $900 million in business loans after both acquisitions close.
Shares of Sovereign closed Tuesday unchanged at 15-1/6. Those of Fleet Financial closed unchanged at 63-3/8.
